title: Year-end planning: 10 actions to consider before 2027 - J.P. Morgan Private Bank
content:
We work with a variety of clients to help them achieve their unique ambitions. We work with a variety of clients to help them achieve their unique ambitions. Our world-class economists, strategists, and investment specialists share their timely ideas and perspectives. We have worked with clients for more than 200 years to help them achieve their unique ambitions. Are you doing everything you can to enhance your financial well-being—and help manage your 2026 taxes? Careful review of your financial picture before year end can help you make the most of these 10 planning strategies in 2027 and beyond. Having ample time to review your balance sheet and your personal and financial goals for the coming year will allow you to make thoughtful adjustments before January 1, if needed. An early start will also make it easier to involve your personal and professional advisors in the process. Establish or update a structured decision-making framework for your investments and goals. This can help provide clarity and consistency to ensure that your goals are aligned with your financial resources. Ask your J.P. Morgan team about our proprietary Goals-Based planning tool to help analyze your risk exposure and cash flows and position your balance sheet to support your investment, spending and gifting objectives and make decisions. We expect the Federal Reserve to hike interest rates once this year, by 25 basis points, before holding rates steady for some time. Short-duration instruments and laddered structures can potentially offer attractive yields today while keeping you positioned to extend when yields peak. Other planning moves to consider: Review all policies, including term coverage, to make sure they still meet the initial intent and if any changes need to be made.  Among the things to review, check: Ask your accountant for an approximation of what your 2026 taxes due will be, based on the information to date. This “pro forma” can inform decisions about whether to accelerate or delay the recognition of deductible items. Consider asking your J.P. Morgan team for a “tax summary”, based on your account information to help with your tax estimates. With your tax snapshot in hand, you can better assess if it makes sense to implement tax planning strategies before year-end. Consider harvesting tax losses (and maybe some gains) Tax-loss harvesting is a classic strategy that may reduce your tax liability.1 Tax loss harvesting involves selling an investment at a loss. This loss can help offset either already-realized gains, or embedded gains that you realize now or in the future. Be careful not to violate any “wash sale rule” in your home jurisdiction. Such rules may prevent investors from taking a loss if they buy a substantially identical or similar security within a certain amount of time before or after the trade. Some countries already impose wealth or inheritance taxes, while others have been discussing them for years. Now is a good time to look at your balance sheet and decide if there are assets you want to transfer to younger family members or to charity. You may  consider whether irrevocable trusts are appropriate for your family members.2 These trusts may be for children and grandchildren, or continue for many generations. Speak with your attorneys and your J.P. Morgan wealth advisor about strategies to transfer wealth to the next generation. Review existing estate planning documents, such as wills and trusts, to confirm they reflect your current wishes and family circumstances. Carefully plan trust distributions to ensure they’re as tax efficient as possible. If making gifts to family members living in the U.S., be mindful of gifting any U.S. tangible property, including cash, which could trigger U.S. gift tax. For charitable gifts, review your year-end gifting strategy and whether you can take a charitable deduction for your gifts. There are many ways to give to charity, from direct gifts, to donor advised funds, or your own foundation. Establishing a plan for giving can help your charitable dollars have the most impact. Keep in mind that some assets may take longer to transfer. Make sure any donation process begins early enough to be deemed complete by December 31. It's never too early to begin talking with your children and grandchildren about money, family values, and the responsibilities that can come with wealth.  These conversations do not need to be formal or overly complex.  They can begin in simple, natural ways — a discussion around the dinner table, sharing stories behind the family’s history, talking about how wealth can support a meaningful life, or by choosing a charitable gift together. Year-end gatherings can provide a good opportunity to be more intentional, turning time together into a chance to strengthen communication, build understanding, and help younger generations feel more prepared over time. For some families, this may evolve into a more structured family meeting; for others, the goal may simply be to create a regular rhythm of open and honest communication. Either way, these moments can help build trust, confidence, and a sense of shared purpose well before any formal transfer of responsibility takes place. As Artificial Intelligence (AI) apps and tools continue to become integrated into daily life, it's crucial to actively protect your data and privacy, especially from social engineering threats. Here are steps to take now: With an active IPO market in 2026, many families are navigating significant new liquidity events—or preparing for ones on the horizon. Whether you are part of a company that recently completed its IPO, hold stock in a pre-IPO company, or manage a portfolio heavily weighted to a single position, this is the time to evaluate your exposure and goals. Depending on your restrictions and tax situation, consider 10b5-1 trading plans, or charitable strategies to help manage single-stock risk in a tax-efficient manner. If you received new equity awards this year, review the vesting schedule, the tax treatment at vesting versus exercise and whether you have awards approaching expiration that require action. If you were granted stock options, understand the financial impact of exercising your options and develop an exercise strategy before the options expire. For those with post-IPO lockup expirations approaching, consider your options and liquidity needs, and develop a plan early to make decisions based on your ultimate intent. These are just a few examples of the many opportunities you may have right now to strengthen your financial health before year-end. Ask your J.P. Morgan team for help analyzing the opportunities and risks across your balance sheet. They will work closely with you and your other professional advisors to help you bring 2026 to a close and prepare for the year ahead. The sooner you have these discussions, the more benefit you may be able to reap from your year-end planning. Morgan reiterated its Buy rating and $200 price target on Oracle on Nov. 23, 83% above the stock's latest close. Oracle has paid for its AI data centers with new stock and debt, and OpenAI, which S&P says is about half its backlog, is still raising money. The cost of insuring Oracle's debt hit a record this week, alongside CoreWeave's, so funding is still the main risk. On fiscal 2028 earnings estimates, $200 is 18x, below Oracle's five-year average of 21x, which makes J.P. Morgan's target a reasonable one. Oracle (ORCL:NYSE) closed at $109.51 on Nov. 24, 56% below its June 1 high. But on Nov. 23, J.P. Morgan analyst Samik Chatterjee reiterated his Buy rating and $200 price target, 83% above that close. He's held that target since August, when it sat about 30% above the stock's $153.28. In the quarter that ended Aug. 31, Oracle's revenue rose 30% to $19.3 billion, but capital spending hit $28.5 billion and free cash flow was negative $5 billion. Oracle sold $20 billion of stock to help pay for it, then raised about $10 billion more in stock and $10 billion in notes on Nov. 2. S&P says OpenAI accounts for about half of Oracle's backlog, while OpenAI's latest funding round has reached only half of its $30 billion target, CNBC reported. In August, J.P. Morgan projected that Oracle's revenue would grow about 33% a year and its EPS about 29% a year through fiscal 2030. It argued that growth should earn Oracle a multiple closer to its AI infrastructure peers'. It reiterated the call the day Oracle's stock jumped on the company's statement that its OpenAI contract is fully funded. Others have pulled back: DBS cut its target to $290 from $310 on Nov. 12, keeping its Buy, and analysts' average target has fallen from $349 a year ago to $236: That's still 136% above the price. Of the eight firms that weighed in this month, J.P. Morgan has the lowest target. TIKR tracks 42 analysts on Oracle. How many say "Buy"? See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Oracle, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Oracle's Analyst Ratings Analysts expect normalized EPS of $11.06 in fiscal 2028, which ends in May 2028, up from $10.91 three months ago: On that $11.06, $200 is 18x earnings (our math: J.P. Morgan hasn't published its method). Oracle trades at 13x forward earnings today, against a five-year average of 21x: So the target needs 30% earnings growth, which analysts already expect, and a multiple that rises from 13x to 18x. That's hardly heroic. Oracle traded between 12x and 17x from 2014 to early 2021, when its revenue grew about 1% a year, and analysts now expect revenue to nearly double from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2028. The catch is the debt. Oracle says free cash flow tops $30 billion in fiscal 2029, while analysts expect $17.5 billion. And on Nov. 25, the cost of insuring Oracle's debt hit a record, alongside CoreWeave (CRWV:NASDAQ), whose spread implies a 68% chance of default within five years. Until credit markets stop lumping the two together, a higher multiple will be hard to earn. Still, I think J.P. Morgan has this one right. Its $200 needs a multiple below Oracle's five-year average, on estimates that are still edging up. If the funding holds, 18x a year out is a reasonable landing spot. Oracle's second-quarter report in mid-December is the next test. Non-GAAP EPS within its $1.85-$1.93 guide, with non-GAAP operating margin holding near the first quarter's 42%, would back the call. title: JP Morgan Outlines Oil Outlook for 2027, 2028 - Rigzone
content:
In a new report sent to Rigzone by Natasha Kaneva, J.P. Morgan’s Head of Global Commodities Strategy, analysts at the company, including Kaneva, outlined J.P. Morgan’s oil outlook for 2027 and 2028. The J.P. Morgan analysts revealed in the report that their outlook assumes the U.S.-Iran and Russia-Ukraine conflicts continue, “yet oil keeps moving and the global market remains in surplus”. “If 2022 and 2026 have taught us anything, it is that wars can disrupt oil flows without stopping them,” the analysts said in the report. “We are therefore modeling a world in which two wars continue, but oil keeps moving,” they added. The analysts highlighted in the report that, “with crude flowing and demand contracting, the global oil market returned to surplus in September”. They pointed out that this excess widened in October and that China has already begun rebuilding its crude inventories, “adding 400,000 barrels per day in October” with the country “on pace to add another 500,000 barrels per day in November”. “We expect that surplus to persist into 2027,” the analysts revealed. “Our forecast assumes Middle Eastern oil flows remain near 90 percent of pre-war levels through March, rising to 94 percent by June and 98 percent by year-end, while demand returns sustainably to pre-war volumes by August,” they added. “China is expected to rebuild crude inventories at an average pace of nearly 700,000 barrels per day, with OECD countries adding another 400,000 barrels per day,” they projected. They warned, however, that, even after accounting for this stock-building, they project a global surplus of 1.6 million barrels per day, “consistent with a Brent price in the high $70s in the first half of the year and the high $60s in the second”. The analysts went on to warn that this surplus will not disappear in 2028. “Even assuming China accelerates inventory accumulation to 1.1 million barrels per day and OECD countries continue adding 0.4 million barrels per day, we expect the market to remain oversupplied by roughly 1.4 million barrels per day, implying a Brent price in the mid-$60s,” they said. “That is our fundamentally driven price forecast, not necessarily the price at which oil will trade throughout the year,” the analysts highlighted, noting that further escalations “could inject substantial geopolitical risk premia into the market”. The J.P. Morgan analysts revealed in the report that they are reluctant to forecast those premia, “let alone embed them permanently into our price outlook”. “History suggests they can be large, but rarely last,” they pointed out. “Since 2005, monthly Brent prices have never exceeded our estimated fair value by more than $24 per barrel, with such deviations lasting an average of just 3.8 months,” they said. “Two wars may keep oil prices volatile. But unless they materially alter the physical balance, the underlying surplus should ultimately prevail,” they projected. The J.P. Morgan analysts highlighted in the report that a “flood of supply is coming”, pointing out that global liquids production “is projected to surge by nearly eight million barrels per day in 2027, reaching 109 million barrels per day, before climbing to 110 million barrels per day by year-end and remaining near that level in 2028”. In their report, the analysts outlined that the U.S.-Iran conflict “has acted like a dam, holding back Middle Eastern production for months”. “Once the barriers are lifted, the rush to reclaim lost market share could unleash a flood of additional supply, particularly from producers outside Iran,” they projected. “By March 2027, we expect Middle Eastern supply outside of Iran to have fully recovered to its 2025 average, before rising further,” they said. The Middle East will not be alone in driving supply growth, according to the analysts, who projected that the Americas are set to add another 1.6 million barrels per day to supply, led by a 0.5 million barrel per day increase in U.S. total liquids production. “Brazil should contribute another 0.5 million barrels per day, as three new floating production, storage and offloading vessels come online, with output expected to keep rising through 2031,” they said. “Guyana should add 0.3 million barrels per day, while Canada and Argentina will contribute another 0.1 and 0.2 million barrels per day, respectively,” they added. “Importantly, much of the growth in Brazil and Guyana comes from deep-water projects, where production is relatively insensitive to oil prices and unlikely to slow even if prices weaken,” they continued. The analysts went on to warn that Russia “remains the main geopolitical variable”. “Assuming the war in Ukraine continues without a resolution, we expect Russian production to average 8.7 million barrels per day next year, broadly unchanged from current levels,” they said. “A ceasefire, however, could lift output to 9.4 million barrels per day, adding another 0.7 million barrels per day to global supply,” they added. “Put these numbers together, and the scale of the recovery becomes extraordinary. After plunging from 107 million barrels per day in 2025 to 101 million barrels per day in 2026, global liquids production is poised to surge to 109 million barrels per day in 2027,” they noted. “That is nearly eight million barrels per day of additional supply in a single year, more than reversing the losses of 2026 and leaving the world producing two million barrels per day more oil than before the war,” they added. “In just twelve months, the world could emerge from one of the largest supply disruptions in history with more oil than it had going into it,” they continued. “And the recovery is unlikely to stop there”, the analysts emphasized. “We project global oil supply to reach 110 million barrels per day by the end of 2027 and remain near that level throughout 2028 - some three million barrels per day above its 2025 average and an extraordinary nine million barrels per day above 2019 levels,” they added. The J.P. Morgan analysts projected in the report that oil demand will rebound but said refining capacity will set the ceiling for this comeback. “Oil consumption could theoretically recover by 4.5 million barrels per day in 2027 but meeting that demand would require global refinery runs to increase by 4.1 million barrels per day relative to 2026, against an expected gain of just 3.3 million barrels per day,” they said. “Refining constraints will keep product cracks and prices elevated, limiting demand growth to 3.5 million barrels per day, just 0.6 million barrels per day above pre-war levels,” they added. The analysts went on to reveal in the report that, “with demand data now available through September”, they estimate that global oil consumption has fallen by 3.0 million barrels per day this year. “Nearly half of that decline - 1.3 million barrels per day - came from petrochemical feedstocks, as physical shortages forced refiners to cut runs, particularly in Asia,” they said. “The rest was largely a response to record-high regional prices for refined products, rather than crude oil itself, with diesel demand falling by 0.8 million barrels per day, gasoline by 0.5 million barrels per day and jet fuel by 0.1 million barrels per day,” they added. “The Middle East, at the center of the conflict, saw consumption fall by 0.9 million barrels per day, while China and the rest of Asia each lost roughly 0.8 million barrels per day as shortages and soaring product prices took their toll,” they continued. “The impact eventually spread to developed economies, including Europe, where consumption contracted by 0.28 million barrels per day and the U.S., where it declined by 0.13 million barrels per day,” they noted. The analysts stated in the report that “why consumption fell matters enormously for what comes next”. “If demand has fallen primarily because oil products were unavailable or prohibitively expensive, much of that consumption should return once supplies normalize and prices retreat,” they said. “And although the conflict is now in its ninth month, we doubt it has lasted long enough to fundamentally reshape consumption patterns,” they added. “Still, there is a limit to how much stretching even a rubber band can withstand. The longer consumers are forced to adapt to shortages and high prices, the greater the risk that some of those adjustments will become permanent,” they continued. The J.P. Morgan analysts said in the report that, “for now”, their “natural inclination is to follow the conventional logic of hysteresis”. “After major economic shocks and disruptions, oil consumption tends to recover toward its previous level, but the subsequent growth trajectory becomes shallower. In other words, the level of demand recovers, but some of its future growth is lost,” they added. The mechanism for that recovery is relatively straightforward, according to the analysts. “As damaged refining capacity returns and refinery runs normalize, product shortages should ease, refining cracks should retreat and trade flows recover,” they said. “Lower product prices, in turn, should encourage consumption that was previously constrained by either availability or affordability,” they added. “Following this logic, global oil demand could in theory rebound like a coiled spring, surging by as much as 4.5 million barrels per day in 2027, lifting consumption 1.5 million barrels per day above its pre-war level,” they continued. “But here is the rub - the world may have more than enough crude oil to meet demand, but not enough refining capacity to turn it into the products consumers actually need,” they warned. The analysts highlighted that accommodating the additional 1.5 million barrels per day of consumption would require global refinery runs to increase by 1.1 million barrels per day relative to 2025. “Yet global refining capacity is expected to increase by just 0.97 million barrels per day - enough to support an increase in runs of only about 200,000 barrels per day,” they said. “The resulting mismatch between rebounding demand and constrained processing capacity would push gasoline, diesel and jet fuel cracks higher, raising prices for the very products whose soaring costs drove demand down in the first place,” they warned. After accounting for the volume of crude that refiners “can realistically process”, the analysts estimated in the report that global oil demand in 2027 could rise by a maximum of 0.58 million barrels per day above 2025 levels, equivalent to a recovery of 3.5 million barrels per day from 2026. In a BMI report sent to Rigzone by the Fitch Group recently, analysts at BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions, projected that energy prices are set to fall “as scarcity shifts to oversupply, while refined fuel prices remain elevated”. “After a preliminary U.S.-Iran deal is reached, regional oil and gas flows will rise, paving the way for strong gains in global crude and natural gas exports,” the BMI analysts projected in this report. “As supply growth overwhelms demand, the market will tip into surplus, driving steep and broad-based declines in energy prices,” they added. “That said, global fuel prices will stay elevated into 2027 as refining constraints and record-low inventories keep markets undersupplied, despite improving Strait of Hormuz trade flows and possible extra Mainland Chinese exports,” they continued. The analysts warned in the report that the year 2027 will mark a “sharp reversal” for energy commodities, “as fading geopolitical risk premia and a surge in supply drive steep price declines across the complex”. “The U.S.-Iran war has been the dominant factor behind 2026’s rally, and our core view sees Washington and Tehran reach a preliminary deal in Q1 2027, triggering a sharp sell-off in oil and gas prices,” they said. “As the maritime security environment improves and the Strait of Hormuz reopens, regional flows will normalize in full, unlocking volumes constrained since the outbreak of the conflict,” they added. The BMI analysts noted that Middle Eastern Gulf crude oil producers were operating around seven million barrels per day below capacity as of October 2026 and revealed that they are forecasting that regional production will rise by 5.59 million barrels per day year on year in 2027, “alongside a further 2.10 million barrels per day of growth elsewhere, with the U.S. leading the gains”. “That expansion will comfortably outstrip the recovery in oil demand,” they warned. “Lower energy costs, improving economic conditions, higher Asian refinery utilization and the rebuilding of depleted inventories will absorb some of the additional barrels, but only temporarily, while structural trends towards efficiency, fuel-switching and electrification continue to cap consumption growth,” they projected. The analysts revealed in the report that they expect Brent to average $112 per barrel in Q1 2027 before dropping to $67 per barrel by Q4 2027, averaging $81 per barrel over 2027, “down from $93 per barrel in 2026”. They warned, however, that they are already seeing “strong downside risks to this forecast” which they said they are likely to revise down in the coming weeks. “The emerging glut will test OPEC+’s ability to manage the market and, with the imbalance unlikely to clear in 2028, we forecast Brent to average around $70 per barrel over 2028-2030, with risks tilted towards a deeper downturn,” they said in the report. The BMI analysts projected that refined fuels will fall in tandem but forecasted that “the slower recovery in Middle Eastern downstream operations and continued disruption to Russian refining will keep product cracks historically elevated”. “The same dynamics will play out in gas, as recovering Middle Eastern LNG exports coincide with nearly 95 million tons per annum (mtpa) of new liquefaction capacity by end-2027, pushing global gas markets into prolonged surplus,” they noted. In the report, the BMI analysts went on to highlight that global fuel prices are expected to remain elevated as refining capacity constraints continue to limit supply growth against record-low inventories. “The availability of global refined fuels should continue to steadily improve with increased trade flows emanating from the Strait of Hormuz over the early quarters of 2027, although fundamentals will remain tilted to undersupply, full normalization of pre-conflict trade remains elusive, and Russian refining capacity remains disrupted,” they said. “Mainland China’s increasing fuel exports may give markets some additional supply relief, but limited fuel exports to end-2026 hint at continued restraint for 2027,” they warned. “Diesel, gasoline and jet fuel prices are al forecast to ease from their 2026 peaks but remain elevated through 2027 as refining constraints and depleted inventories keep markets undersupplied,” they added. The analysts outlined in the report that a preliminary U.S.-Iran agreement reopening the Strait of Hormuz in Q1 2027 would support a gradual improvement in product availability but said full normalization of pre-conflict trade flows “will take longer given depleted inventories and constrained refining capacity”. “Additional Mainland Chinese fuel exports could offer some supply relief, but limited export volumes to end-2026 point to continued restraint into 2027,” they projected. title: HSBC, J.P. Morgan & StoneX Execute Digital Gold Trade - Markets Media
content:
The World Gold Council announced that HSBC, J.P. Morgan and StoneX have traded, settled and used Pooled Gold Interests (PGI) as collateral in live, legally binding wholesale-market transactions for the first time. The World Gold Council’s Wholesale Digital Gold initiative is underpinned by PGI, and these pilot transactions mark a significant step towards a new way for institutions to own, transfer and use gold. ICE Benchmark Administration (IBA) acted as operator and Baton Systems as technology provider. Loco London physical 400-ounce Good Delivery gold bars were placed into the Wholesale Digital Gold ecosystem and PGI were created, giving participants proprietary interests over pooled gold. Once the transactions were settled, the gold was withdrawn from the ecosystem, completing the full lifecycle. The Wholesale Digital Gold initiative has developed a new settlement ecosystem for the wholesale gold market, now at pilot stage, in which ownership of segregated physical gold is held and transferred electronically as PGI. It aims to address a longstanding challenge for the industry: how to preserve the integrity and trust of physical gold ownership while making gold easier to trade and use across modern financial markets. It is designed to complement existing allocated and unallocated gold settlement. The pilot demonstrates real progress on how digitalisation can help gold move more efficiently through financial markets. It comes as the FCA considers responses to its Call for Input on tokenised gold in UK wholesale markets, including its potential use as collateral. Together, these developments help strengthen the UK’s position to lead the next generation of gold-market infrastructure. Following the pilot, participating institutions commented on the live test of Pooled Gold Interests: David Tait, Chief Executive Officer, World Gold Council, said: “Today, Wholesale Digital Gold moved from concept to reality. For the first time, leading institutions have transferred, settled and used fractional ownership of physical gold as collateral through real, live transactions. This is a historic step forward for the gold market, preserving trust in physical ownership while opening up new ways for gold to be used in modern financial markets. This kind of significant progress can only be achieved when the industry works together.” Richard Anthony, Global Head of Macro eRisk and Precious Metals, HSBC, said: “HSBC has been participating in the precious metals market for more than 160 years and is one of the world’s largest gold custodians and clearers. We continue to invest in technology, including our gold tokenisation capabilities, to enable our clients to have greater access to gold. Developing a modern digital infrastructure for gold ownership and settlement is important to the overall market.” Mark Amlin, Global Head of Physical Commodities, J.P. Morgan, said: “J.P. Morgan is one of the largest and most active participants in the global precious metals market, with a presence that spans trading, clearing, vaulting and financing across every major hub. That global footprint gives us a clear view of where the market’s infrastructure needs to evolve. Gold ownership that is fractional, readily transferable and insolvency remote would allow gold to be used more widely across financial markets, including as collateral. We were pleased to test that in practice alongside other market participants.” Michael Skinner, Global Head of Metals, StoneX, said: “StoneX has invested consistently in developing new solutions across commodities markets, from vaulting and refining through to execution and clearing, and we support initiatives like this one because they have the potential to deliver materially better outcomes for our clients — greater flexibility, lower operational friction and more efficient use of capital. We are pleased to have been involved from the outset.” “IBA has a track record of anticipating and providing the infrastructure that modern commodity and financial markets require to operate more efficiently, including as the administrator of some of the world’s most important precious metals benchmarks. For new collateral and settlement models to scale, they require certainty and predictability. IBA’s experience providing robust and reliable governance, technology and data management, combined with our whole-market approach, helps build confidence amongst participants and other stakeholders in the infrastructure we provide. We are pleased to act as operator for these pilot transactions and to bring our experience to the Wholesale Digital Gold ecosystem.” Arjun Jayaram, Founder and Chief Executive Officer, Baton Systems, said: “Wholesale Digital Gold requires real-time technology with distinct workflows and data permissions for each participant. We have spent a decade building infrastructure that enables institutions to control and move cash, securities and collateral, and digital gold is a natural extension of that work. We were delighted to help show what a modern, interoperable settlement layer can do for one of the world’s oldest and deepest markets.” This initiative has been developed by the World Gold Council, advised by Linklaters LLP and Hilltop Walk Consulting and was first launched in September 2025 in the White Paper: Pooled Gold Interests and Wholesale Digital Gold – A New Vision for the Gold Market. The World Gold Council continues to invite market participants, regulators and technology providers to engage in this initiative and help shape the future of the gold market. title: CME Group imposes $100k fine on J.P. Morgan Securities for alleged COMEX rule violations - FX News Group
content: International derivatives marketplace CME Group has posted a notice of disciplinary action against J.P. Morgan Securities LLC (JPMS). Pursuant to an offer of settlement in which JPMS neither admitted nor denied the rule violations or factual findings upon which the penalty is based, a Panel of the Commodity Exchange (COMEX) Business Conduct Committee found that certain customer agreements with JPMS included a period of time during which the firm’s full discretion to determine when and under what circumstances positions could be liquidated was restricted. In addition, JPMS contractually agreed with certain customers to language on timing, without the ability to accelerate such timing, that limited its ability to call for performance bond collateral. title: HSBC, JP Morgan settle first live digital gold collateral trades - Ledger Insights
content: The World Gold Council announced the first live transactions for Pooled Gold Interests (PGI) between HSBC, JP Morgan and StoneX, a little over a year after it first proposed the concept in a September 2025 white paper. The Wholesale Digital Gold pilot involved trading, settlement and the use of gold as collateral, which is a key driver behind the initiative. ICE Benchmark Administration (IBA) is the platform operator and Baton Systems is the technology provider. Gold is a significant market worth around $28 trillion in total, with around half of that considered investable. About $8 trillion is in the form of physical bars, coins, gold ETFs and over the counter private investments, with central banks managing $5 trillion and derivatives worth more than a trillion. The challenge with physical gold is it sits at custodians, and moving it is not that easy. Yet owners want to use it as collateral, and the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) is exploring how to make that happen. Pooled Gold Interests aim to combine quick transfers with a proprietary interest in the gold, which might make central counterparties (CCPs) more willing to accept it as collateral. It’s not that gold isn’t currently electronically traded. The challenge is the formats. To transfer gold quickly, most is held “unallocated” with a bank, meaning it is a claim on the bank as opposed to outright ownership of the bars. In London those claims are mainly on Citi, HSBC, ICBC Standard Bank, JP Morgan and UBS. Because of the bank counterparty risk, this form of gold is not eligible as CCP collateral in the UK and EU. By contrast there is far less risk if identified gold bars are held at a custodian, but there’s friction in transferring it. This is referred to as “allocated” gold and CME Clearing is one of the few to accept this as collateral. The World Gold Council’s PGI pilot introduces a third path that addresses the counterparty risk while making gold easier to move and settle. The FCA is expressly exploring gold tokenization. Yet the PGI pilot does not use tokens, even though it uses a distributed ledger. Baton Systems told Ledger Insights the PGIs were created on its permissioned DLT, which also handled the transfers, settlement and the collateral pledge. Baton is known for its Core Collateral and Core FX solutions, with HSBC as an anchor client for Core FX, which is now the foundation of OSTTRA’s PvP offering. Core FX likewise uses DLT for workflow purposes rather than tokens, and several years ago HSBC’s Mark Williamson outlined some of the benefits of sidestepping tokenization to Ledger Insights, noting that tokenization can add an extra settlement step and create fragmented liquidity. Since then HSBC has launched its own gold tokenization offering, both for wholesale clients and for retail in Hong Kong. Want the full story? The SOTP valuation method assesses a company's individual divisions separately, using comparable businesses to establish their potential worth. The contrasting revisions reflect stronger earnings expectations alongside a more conservative valuation of part of the business. Rolls-Royce indicated in its November 12 trading update that it would revisit its medium-term targets when it publishes full-year results in February. The group also plans to accelerate its existing share buyback programme from November 2026, bringing forward purchases of its own shares. Tokenization is the process of using blockchain technology to turn real‑world assets (RWAs) such as stocks, real estate, government bonds, etc. into digital tokens, which can be traded fractionally, 24/7. While the stock tokens offer traders from outside the U.S. indirect exposure to the American stock market, they don't offer shareholder rights such as ownership, voting, etc., like original stocks do. The Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC) innovation exemption published in September lets crypto exchanges offer tokenized U.S. stocks without registering as exchanges. title: JP Morgan Supplies $90M Refi for Murray Hill Multifamily Tower - Commercial Observer
content: Brause Realty has secured a $90 million loan to refinance a newly built luxury apartment tower in Midtown East, Commercial Observer has learned. J.P. Morgan Chase provided the loan for the developer’s 157-unit the Lotus property in Manhattan’s Murray Hill neighborhood, a project completed in early 2026. Brause Realty also landed a $75 million construction loan from J.P. Morgan for the project in 2024, CO first reported at the time. Cushman & Wakefield negotiated the refi with a team consisting of Gideon Gil, Zach Kraft, Cecelia Galligan and Crawford Bundy. “The property’s strong leasing performance, exceptional amenities and long-term tax benefits helped secure attractive financing terms, reflecting continued lender demand for well-positioned multifamily properties in New York City,” Gil, executive vice chairman with C&W, said in a statement. Located at 255 East 39th Street, the 20-story property has 109 market-rate apartments and 48 units designated as affordable housing, along with 3,900 square feet of ground-floor retail space. Resident amenities include a rooftop lounge, coworking spaces, a fitness center, a yoga studio, a sports simulator and a screening room. The Brause family acquired properties along Second Avenue and East 39th Street in 1942 before expanding ownership in the ensuing decades and completed assemblage for the project in 2021. “The Lotus represents an important milestone for our family and reflects our long-standing commitment to investing in New York City,” David Brause, president of Brause Realty, said in a statement. “We’re proud to have delivered a premier residential property that brings high-quality housing and exceptional amenities to the Murray Hill neighborhood.” J.P. President Donald Trump's renewed support for limiting U.S. credit-card interest rates to 10% has brought earnings risks into focus for Citigroup C, JPMorgan Chase JPM and Capital One Financial COF. Citigroup runs a large U.S. Consumer Cards business spanning general-purpose and private-label cards, while JPMorgan operates a major card franchise within its Consumer & Community Banking division. Capital One has significant exposure to credit-card lending, particularly following its acquisition of Discover Financial Services. All three companies benefit from interest earned on revolving card balances, leaving them exposed to potential revenue and margin pressures from any mandatory reduction in borrowing rates. On Nov. 21, Trump said he was willing to work with Democrats to impose the cap, reviving a campaign pledge as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January 2027. Senator Elizabeth Warren welcomed the proposal, while Republican Senator Josh Hawley reiterated his support for rate-limiting legislation. The proposal aims to ease household borrowing costs at a time when credit-card debt and interest burdens remain elevated. According to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York data cited in recent reporting, the median credit-card rate was approximately 22.2% in August. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau estimates that cardholders were assessed about $160 billion in interest charges in 2024, up from $105 billion in 2022. Researchers have suggested that a 10% ceiling could save consumers roughly $100 billion annually, although actual savings would depend on the legislation and lenders' responses. Trump first championed the idea during his 2024 presidential campaign and called for a one-year ceiling in January 2026. The proposal stalled amid banking-industry opposition and limited congressional support. Separately, Senators Bernie Sanders and Hawley introduced a bill in February 2025 proposing a five-year 10% cap. A proposed 10% cap on credit-card interest rates could pressure banks' earnings by reducing interest income from revolving balances without a corresponding decline in funding costs, servicing expenses or credit losses. Banks may respond by tightening underwriting standards, reducing credit limits, scaling back rewards or increasing permissible fees. These measures could constrain lending growth, customer spending and profitability. Citigroup faces meaningful exposure through its U.S. Consumer Cards business. As of Sept. 30, 2026, C had $177.9 billion in U.S. credit-card loans, comprising $150.3 billion in general-purpose cards and $27.6 billion in private-label cards. Including international operations, its consolidated consumer credit-card loans totaled approximately $192.5 billion. During the first nine months of 2026, Citigroup's U.S. Consumer Cards segment reported average loans of $176 billion, up 4% year over year. Net interest income increased 5% to $15.72 billion, while total revenues rose 2% to $13.94 billion. However, segment net income declined 4% to $2.44 billion, reflecting elevated operating expenses and credit costs. Card rewards and partner payments totaled $10.15 billion, underscoring the segment's substantial customer engagement costs. A rate cap could undermine further growth by squeezing lending margins and pressuring C's efforts to improve profitability and returns. JPMorgan has a larger credit-card portfolio in absolute terms. As of Sept. 30, 2026, Card Services loans totaled $252.7 billion, up 7% year over year. During the first nine months of 2026, average Card Services loans increased 7% to $244.3 billion. Card Services and Auto revenues rose 14% to $23.80 billion, while credit-card provisions for credit losses totaled $6 billion. Card Services' net charge-offs reached $5.90 billion, with a net charge-off rate of 3.23%. JPM reported company-wide net income of $53 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 20% year over year from $44 billion. Credit-card lending remains an important contributor to its profitability, given the higher yields earned on revolving balances relative to many other lending products. An interest-rate ceiling could constrain card-related revenues and profitability despite continued loan growth. However, its diversified operations across investment banking, markets, asset management and consumer banking provide additional earnings support. Capital One appears particularly vulnerable because of its greater concentration in credit-card lending. As of Sept. 30, 2026, its credit-card loans totaled $276.4 billion, representing nearly 60% of its $462.5 billion total loan portfolio. Domestic credit-card loans accounted for approximately $260.3 billion. Capital One's net interest margin stood at 8.10% in the first nine months of 2026, highlighting the importance of interest earnings to its business model. Its Credit Card business generated net interest income of $28.11 billion and net income of $7.14 billion during the first nine months of 2026. The segment's significant contribution to overall profitability underscores the company's sensitivity to a potential mandatory reduction in credit-card borrowing rates. A 10% cap could significantly compress COF's interest income from revolving balances, limiting its ability to offset funding costs and credit losses. The company's expanded card portfolio following the Discover acquisition further increased its exposure to changes in credit-card pricing regulations. Although Capital One could respond through tighter underwriting, reduced rewards and other cost controls, such actions may affect customer acquisition, spending volumes and long-term growth. For now, the proposal represents an emerging downside risk rather than immediate earnings reset. Capital One appears the most exposed due to its substantial reliance on credit-card lending, while Citigroup faces risks to its ongoing profitability recovery. JPMorgan's diversified earnings base offers comparatively greater resilience, although its sizeable card portfolio remains vulnerable. Overall, all three stocks could face pressure if lawmakers move closer to implementing a binding interest-rate ceiling. title: A silver soup tureen once owned by JP Morgan could fetch $8 million at a Christie's auction - ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
content: A massive silver soup tureen once owned by financier J LONDON -- It's a perfect gift for the host with the most. A huge silver soup tureen once owned by financier J.P. Morgan up for sale, with an estimated price of up to 6 million pounds (almost $8 million). More than a foot and a half long (46 centimeters) long and weighing in at 44 pounds (20 kilograms), the Meissonnier Tureen is the star of a Dec. 1 auction at Christie’s in London. Made in the 1730s by the French artist and goldsmith Juste-Aurèle Meissonnier in a flamboyant rococo style, it was “designed to astonish,” according to Christie’s specialist Isabelle Cartier-Stone. Shaped like a stylized shell, it has a cover encrusted with detailed silver plants and animals, including “a duck, a crab, a fish, an oyster, and a snail among an artichoke and other leafy vegetables,” according to the catalog. The tureen’s owners have included British aristocrats, Russian statesmen and the American banker John Pierpont Morgan. It is one of a pair split up after they were auctioned together in 1977, with the other in the Cleveland Museum of Art in Ohio. It is being sold as part of a trove of silver owned by the Blaquier-Arrieta family of wealthy Argentine collectors and has a presale estimate of between 4 million pounds and 6 million pounds ($5.25 million and $7.86 million). A group of a dozen paintings owned by the same family sold at Sotheby’s last week for $412 million, with the Vincent van Gogh painting “Châtaigniers en fleurs” (Chestnut Trees in Flower) fetching $190.4 million. title: JP Morgan says Barclays shares are a Buy with the potential to rise 41% - Yahoo Finance UK
content: Tip: Try a valid symbol or a specific company name for relevant results Barclays' (LSE: BARC) shares stand out to me as cheap right now. And I'm clearly not the only one who believes they're undervalued at the moment. Recently, analysts at JP Morgan – who have an Overweight (Buy) rating on the stock – stuck a 580p price target on the shares. That's a whopping 41% above the current share price. It's easy to see why JP Morgan's analysts believe Barclays' shares can move significantly higher over the next 12 months. Today, they trade at a very low valuation. Looking at the consensus earnings per share forecast for 2027 (62.4p), the forward-looking price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio's only 6.6. For reference, Lloyds is trading at 8.4, HSBC at 9.2, and NatWest at 7.4. Zooming in on the price-to-tangible-book-value ratio, it's just 0.8. This tells us that the market's valuing the company at 20% below its net tangible assets, meaning that if you stripped out goodwill and other intangibles, the price is still lower than what's left on the balance sheet. For reference here, Lloyds, HSBC, and NatWest have ratios of 1.2, 1.5, and 1.2, respectively. So Barclays is substantially cheaper than its UK peers by this metric. Of course, it's worth asking why the shares are so cheap. I see a few reasons. One is that Barclays is a complex bank with many moving parts. Not only does it offer regular retail and commercial banking, but it also does investment banking and securities trading. Personally, I see this as a plus as it means the bank has multiple ways to make money. But performance in investment banking and trading can be volatile and the exposure here seems to spook a lot of investors. Another reason is that the bank's a major player in the credit card space in the US. Unsecured credit card debt's the first thing consumers typically default on during an economic slowdown, so the market prices in higher cyclical credit risk compared to other banks that are more focused on mortgages. A third reason is that the bank offers a lower dividend yield than some of its peers. At present, the yield here is only around 3.7% versus 4.8%, 4.9%, 6.3% for Lloyds, HSBC, and NatWest, respectively. It's no secret that UK investors tend to prize high yields. Therefore, the lower yield may be turning some investors off. So there are a few issues to consider here and the shares do have risks and disadvantages. However, with the bank engaged in a cost-cutting drive, and aggressively rolling out new technology – specifically focusing on generative and agentic AI, cloud data modernisation, and automated developer tools – I see quite a bit of potential in the medium term.
